subject.title: [Bug]: Performance degradation in session memory sync: full delete-reinsert pattern for growing JSONL files

question: Should maintainers pursue a fresh current-main incremental session indexing implementation, rescue the conflicting open candidate PR, or intentionally keep full-entry reindex behavior for correctness?
rationale: The choice affects memory schema behavior, batching semantics, overlap handling, compaction fallback, and whether the existing candidate branch is worth adopting.

options.title: Fresh current-main fix
options.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current memory-core schema and source-wide batching paths, with overlap and compaction fallback tests.

options.title: Rescue the open PR
options.body: Ask the contributor or a maintainer to rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75179 and replace obsolete assumptions before review continues.

options.title: Keep full reindex
options.body: Leave the current behavior if maintainers decide session-memory correctness is worth the repeated long-transcript indexing cost.

recommendation.title: Fresh current-main fix
recommendation.body: Implement incremental session indexing against the current memory-core schema and source-wide batching paths, with overlap and compaction fallback tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent storage/schema work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the schema-sensitive design choice.
